verses.1:1: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,
verses.1:2: "The Lord was angry with your fathers with great wrath.
verses.1:3: And you shall say to them, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, says the Lord of hosts, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts.
verses.1:4: And do not become like your fathers, to whom the former prophets called out, saying, "Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and from your evil practices." Yet they did not listen, and they did not give heed to listen to Me, says the Lord.
verses.1:5: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, shall they live forever?
verses.1:6: Nevertheless, receive My words and My statutes, all that I command by My Spirit to My servants the prophets, who overtook your fathers. And they answered and said, "Just as the Lord Almighty has purposed to do to us according to our ways and according to our practices, so He has done to us."'"
verses.1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying:
verses.1:8: I saw by night, and behold, a man mounted upon a red horse, and he stood between the shady mountains, and behind him were red, speckled gray, spotted, and white horses.
verses.1:9: And I said, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who spoke within me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
verses.1:10: And the man who stood between the mountains answered and said to me, "These are those whom the Lord has sent out to patrol the earth."
verses.1:11: And they answered the angel of the Lord who stood between the mountains and said, "We have patrolled all the earth, and behold, all the earth is inhabited and is at rest."
verses.1:12: And the angel of the Lord answered and said, "O Lord Almighty, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which You have overlooked this seventieth year?"
verses.1:13: And the Lord Almighty answered the angel who spoke within me with good words and words of comfort.
verses.1:14: And the angel who spoke within me said to me, "Cry out, saying, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy,
verses.1:15: and with great wrath I am angry against the nations that join in attacking; because while I was angry a little, they joined in for evil.
verses.1:16: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will look upon Jerusalem with compassion, and My house shall be rebuilt in her, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure shall yet be stretched out over Jerusalem.'"
verses.1:17: And the angel who spoke within me said to me, "Cry out, saying, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: Cities shall yet overflow with good things, and the Lord shall yet have mercy on Zion, and shall choose Jerusalem.'"
verses.2:1: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, four horns.
verses.2:2: And I said to the angel who spoke within me, "What are these, my lord?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel and Jerusalem."
verses.2:3: And the Lord showed me four craftsmen.
verses.2:4: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah and shattered Israel, and none of them lifted up his head; and these have come forth to sharpen them into their hands—the four horns, the nations that lift up a horn against the land of the Lord to scatter it."
verses.2:5: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a man, and in his hand was a measuring line.
verses.2:6: And I said to him, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how great her width is and how great her length."
verses.2:7: And behold, the angel who spoke within me stood still, and another angel was coming forth to meet him,
verses.2:8: and he said to him, "Run and speak to that young man, saying, 'Jerusalem shall be fruitfully inhabited because of the multitude of men and livestock in her midst.
verses.2:9: And I will be to her, says the Lord, a wall of fire all around, and I will be for glory in her midst.'"
verses.2:10: "Ah, ah! Flee from the land of the north, says the Lord; for from the four winds of heaven I will gather you, says the Lord.
verses.2:11: Escape to Zion, you who dwell in the daughter of Babylon!"
verses.2:12: For thus says the Lord Almighty: "After glory He has sent Me against the nations that plundered you; for he who touches you is as one who touches the apple of His eye.
verses.2:13: For behold, I bring My hand upon them, and they shall become plunder for those who serve them; and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent Me."
verses.2:14: "Delight and rejoice, O daughter of Zion; for behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, says the Lord.
verses.2:15: And many nations shall flee for refuge to the Lord in that day, and they shall be to Him for a people, and they shall dwell in your midst; and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent Me to you."
verses.2:16: And the Lord shall inherit Judah as His portion upon the holy land, and He shall yet choose Jerusalem.
verses.2:17: Let all flesh be reverent before the face of the Lord, for He has risen up from His holy clouds.
verses.3:1: And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and the devil stood at his right hand to oppose him.
verses.3:2: And the Lord said to the devil, "The Lord rebuke you, O devil, and the Lord who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Behold, is this not like a brand plucked from the fire?"
verses.3:3: And Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel.
verses.3:4: And he answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, "Take away the filthy garments from him." And he said to him, "Behold, I have taken away your iniquities; and clothe him with a full-length robe,
verses.3:5: and set a clean turban upon his head." And they set a clean turban upon his head and clothed him with garments; and the angel of the Lord stood by.
verses.3:6: And the angel of the Lord solemnly testified to Joshua, saying,
verses.3:7: "Thus says the Lord Almighty: You walk in My ways and shall keep watch in My ordinances, and you shall judge My house; and if you diligently guard My court, then I will give you those who walk about in the midst of these who stand here.
verses.3:8: Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men who observe signs; for behold, I am bringing My servant, the Dayspring.
verses.3:9: For the stone that I have set before Joshua—upon the one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I am digging a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will feel out all the unrighteousness of that land in one day.
verses.3:10: In that day, says the Lord Almighty, you shall each invite his neighbor under a vine and under a fig tree."
verses.4:1: And the angel who spoke in me returned and roused me, just as when a man is awakened out of his sleep.
verses.4:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I have seen, and behold, a lampstand all of gold, and the lamp bowl upon it, and seven lamps upon it, and seven funnels for the lamps that are upon it,
verses.4:3: and two olive trees above it, one on the right of its lamp bowl and one on the left."
verses.4:4: And I inquired and spoke to the angel who spoke in me, saying, "What are these things, lord?"
verses.4:5: And the angel who spoke in me answered and spoke to me, saying, "Do you not know what these things are?" And I said, "No, lord."
verses.4:6: And he answered and spoke to me, saying, "This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying, 'Not by great might, nor by strength, but by My Spirit,' says the Lord Almighty.
verses.4:7: 'Who are you, O great mountain before the face of Zerubbabel, to prosper? And I will bring forth the stone of the inheritance, an equality of grace, even grace for it.'"
verses.4:8: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.4:9: "The hands of Zerubbabel laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall complete it; and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
verses.4:10: For who has despised small days? And they shall rejoice and see the stone of tin in the hand of Zerubbabel; these are seven eyes that look upon all the earth."
verses.4:11: And I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on the left?"
verses.4:12: And I inquired a second time and said to him, "What are the two branches of the olive trees that are in the hands of the two golden nozzles, which pour into and supply the golden funnels?"
verses.4:13: And he said to me, "Do you not know what these things are?" And I said, "No, lord."
verses.4:14: And he said, "These two sons of fatness stand before the Lord of all the earth."
verses.5:1: And I turned and lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, a flying sickle.
verses.5:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying sickle, twenty cubits in length and ten cubits in width."
verses.5:3: And he said to me, "This is the curse that goes forth over the face of all the earth; for every thief shall be punished by this even to death, and every perjurer shall be punished by this.
verses.5:4: 'And I will bring it forth,' says the Lord Almighty, 'and it shall enter into the house of the thief and into the house of the one who swears by My name falsely; and it shall lodge in the midst of his house, and it shall consume it, along with its timber and its stones.'"
verses.5:5: And the angel who spoke in me came forth and said to me, "Look up with your eyes and see this thing that goes forth."
verses.5:6: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the measure that goes forth." And he said, "This is their iniquity in all the earth."
verses.5:7: And behold, a talent of lead was lifted up; and behold, one woman was sitting in the midst of the measure.
verses.5:8: And he said, "This is lawlessness." And he cast her into the midst of the measure, and he cast the stone of lead into her mouth.
verses.5:9: And I lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, two women were coming forth, and wind was in their wings; and they had wings of a hoopoe, and they took up the measure between the earth and the heaven.
verses.5:10: And I said to the angel who spoke in me, "Where are they carrying away the measure?"
verses.5:11: And he said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Babylon and to make preparation; and they shall set it there upon its prepared base."
verses.6:1: And I turned and lifted up my eyes and looked, and behold, four chariots coming forth from the midst of two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
verses.6:2: In the first chariot were red horses, and in the second chariot were black horses,
verses.6:3: and in the third chariot were white horses, and in the fourth chariot were dappled, ash-gray horses.
verses.6:4: And I answered and said to the angel who spoke in me, "What are these things, lord?"
verses.6:5: And the angel who spoke in me answered and said, "These are the four winds of heaven; they go forth to stand before the Lord of all the earth."
verses.6:6: As for the one in which the black horses were, they went forth to the land of the north, and the white ones went forth behind them, and the dappled ones went forth to the land of the south,
verses.6:7: and the ash-gray ones went forth and looked to go and patrol the earth. And he said, "Go and patrol the earth." And they patrolled the earth.
verses.6:8: And they cried out, and he spoke to me, saying, "Behold, those who go forth to the land of the north have indeed quieted My wrath in the land of the north."
verses.6:9: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.6:10: "Take the things from the captivity, from the rulers and from its worthy men and from those who have known it, and you shall enter on that day into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, who has come from Babylon;
verses.6:11: and you shall take silver and gold and make crowns, and set them upon the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest;
verses.6:12: and you shall say to him, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: Behold, a Man—Dayspring is His name, and from beneath Him He shall spring up, and He shall build the house of the Lord;
verses.6:13: and He shall receive excellence, and shall sit and rule upon His throne; and the priest shall be at His right hand, and a counsel of peace shall be between both of them.'
verses.6:14: And the crown shall be for those who endure, and for its worthy men, and for those who have known it, and for the favor of the son of Zephaniah, and for a psalm in the house of the Lord.
verses.6:15: And those who are far from them shall come and build in the house of the Lord, and you shall know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you. And this shall come to pass, if you diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God."
verses.7:1: And it came to pass in the fourth year of Darius the king, that the word of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev.
verses.7:2: And Sharezer and Arbeseer the king and his men sent to Bethel to appease the Lord,
verses.7:3: speaking to the priests who were in the house of the Lord Almighty and to the prophets, saying, "The sanctification has entered here in the fifth month, just as it has done already for many years."
verses.7:4: Then the word of the Lord of hosts came to me, saying,
verses.7:5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'If you fast or mourn in the fifth or in the seventh months, and behold, for seventy years, have you indeed fasted a fast to Me?
verses.7:6: And if you eat or drink, is it not you who eat and drink?
verses.7:7: Are not these the words which the Lord spoke through the hands of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, along with her cities round about, and the hill country and the lowland were inhabited?'"
verses.7:8: Then the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying:
verses.7:9: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Judge righteous judgment, and show mercy and compassion, each one to his brother.
verses.7:10: Do not oppress the widow and the fatherless, the sojourner and the poor, and let none of you bear a grudge for the evil of his brother in your hearts.
verses.7:11: Yet they refused to give heed, and turned a senseless back, and made their ears heavy so as not to hear.
verses.7:12: And they set their heart to be disobedient, so as not to hear My law and the words which the Lord Almighty sent by His Spirit through the hands of the former prophets; and great wrath came from the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:13: And it shall come to pass that just as He spoke and they did not listen, so they shall cry out and I will by no means listen," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:14: "And I will cast them out among all the nations which they did not know, and the land shall be laid waste behind them, without anyone passing through or returning; for they have turned a choice land into desolation."
verses.8:1: And the word of the Lord Almighty came, saying:
verses.8:2: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "I have been jealous for Jerusalem and Zion with great jealousy, and with great wrath I have been jealous for her."
verses.8:3: Thus says the Lord: "I will return to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem shall be called the True City, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty, the Holy Mountain."
verses.8:4: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Elderly men and elderly women shall yet sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each one having his staff in his hand because of the multitude of days.
verses.8:5: And the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls playing in her streets."
verses.8:6: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "If it shall be impossible in the sight of the remnant of this people in those days, shall it also be impossible in My sight?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.8:7: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Behold, I am saving My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west,
verses.8:8: and I will bring them in, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they shall be to Me a people, and I will be to them God, in truth and in righteousness."
verses.8:9: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets, from the day that the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and the temple from the time it was built.
verses.8:10: For before those days the wages of men shall be of no profit, and there shall be no wages for beasts, and for him who goes out and him who comes in there shall be no peace from affliction; and I will send forth all men, each one against his neighbor.
verses.8:11: Yet now I am not dealing with the remnant of this people as in the former days," says the Lord Almighty,
verses.8:12: "but rather I will show peace: the vine shall yield its fruit, and the earth shall yield its produce, and the heaven shall give its dew; and I will give all these things as an inheritance to the remnant of this My people.
verses.8:13: And it shall come to pass that just as you were under a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will deliver you thoroughly, and you shall be in blessing. Take courage, and be strong in your hands."
verses.8:14: For thus says the Lord Almighty: "Just as I purposed to bring harm upon you when your fathers provoked Me to anger," says the Lord Almighty, "and I did not relent,
verses.8:15: so I have resolved and purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Take courage!
verses.8:16: These are the things which you shall do: speak truth each one to his neighbor; judge truth and peaceful judgment in your gates;
verses.8:17: and let none of you devise evil against his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love a false oath; for all these things I have hated," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.8:18: And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me.
verses.8:19: The Lord Almighty says: "The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth, and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth shall become to the house of Judah joy and gladness and good feasts; and you shall rejoice, and love truth and peace."
verses.8:20: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Many peoples and the inhabitants of many cities shall yet come,
verses.8:21: and the inhabitants of five cities shall assemble into one city, saying, 'Let us go to implore the face of the Lord and to seek the face of the Lord Almighty; I myself will go as well.'
verses.8:22: And many peoples and many nations shall come to seek the face of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem, and to appease the face of the Lord."
verses.8:23: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "In those days, if ten men from all the languages of the nations take hold, they shall indeed take hold of the hem of a Jewish man, saying, 'We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.'"
verses.9:1: The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Sedrach, and Damascus is His sacrifice; for the Lord watches over men and all the tribes of Israel,
verses.9:2: and in Hamath within her borders; Tyre and Sidon, because they were exceedingly wise.
verses.9:3: And Tyre built strongholds for herself, and treasured up silver like dust, and gold like the mire of the streets.
verses.9:4: And therefore the Lord shall take possession of them, and He shall strike her power into the sea, and she herself shall be consumed with fire.
verses.9:5: Ashkelon shall see and be afraid, and Gaza also, and she shall be in great anguish, and Ekron, because she has been put to shame over her transgression; and a king shall perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon shall by no means be inhabited.
verses.9:6: And foreigners shall dwell in Ashdod, and I will pull down the arrogance of the Philistines,
verses.9:7: and I will take away their blood from their mouth, and their abominations from between their teeth; and these also shall be left as a remnant for our God, and they shall be like a commander of a thousand in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusite.
verses.9:8: And I will set up a bulwark for My house, so that none may pass through nor return, and no one driving them out shall come upon them anymore; for now I have seen with My own eyes.
verses.9:9: Rejoice exceedingly, O daughter of Zion; proclaim aloud, O daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King comes to you; righteous and saving is He, gentle and mounted upon a beast of burden and a young colt.
verses.9:10: And He shall utterly destroy chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war shall be utterly destroyed, and there shall be abundance and peace from the nations; and He shall rule over the waters to the sea, and over the rivers to the outlets of the earth.
verses.9:11: And you, by the blood of your covenant, have sent forth your prisoners out of a pit that has no water.
verses.9:12: You shall dwell in strongholds, O prisoners of the congregation, and in place of one day of your sojourning I will repay you double.
verses.9:13: For I have bent you, O Judah, as a bow for Myself; I have filled Ephraim, and I will stir up your children, O Zion, against the children of the Greeks, and I will handle you like the sword of a warrior.
verses.9:14: And the Lord shall be over them, and an arrow shall go forth like lightning; and the Lord Almighty shall sound with a trumpet, and shall march in the tumult of His threat.
verses.9:15: The Lord Almighty shall shield them; and they shall consume them, and bury them with slingstones, and drink them down like wine, and fill the bowls like an altar.
verses.9:16: And the Lord their God shall save them in that day, His people as sheep; for holy stones are rolled upon His land.
verses.9:17: For whatever good belongs to Him, and whatever beauty belongs to Him—grain for the young men, and fragrant wine for the maidens.
verses.10:1: Ask rain from the Lord in season, both early and late; the Lord has made manifestations, and He will give them winter rain, to each one vegetation in the field.
verses.10:2: For those who utter oracles spoke troubles, and the diviners, false visions; they spoke false dreams and comforted in vain. Therefore they withered away like sheep and were afflicted, because there was no healing.
verses.10:3: "Against the shepherds My wrath was provoked, and I will bring visitation upon the lambs; and the Lord God Almighty will visit His flock, the house of Judah, and will array them as His majestic horse in battle.
verses.10:4: And from him He looked, and from him He arrayed, and from him came a bow in wrath; from him shall go forth everyone who drives out together.
verses.10:5: And they shall be like warriors trampling mire in the streets in battle, and they shall draw up in battle array, because the Lord is with them; and the riders on horses shall be put to shame.
verses.10:6: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will settle them, because I have loved them; and they shall be as though I had not turned away from them, for I am the Lord their God, and I will hear them.
verses.10:7: And they shall be like the warriors of Ephraim, and their heart shall rejoice as with wine; and their children shall see and be glad, and their heart shall rejoice in the Lord.
verses.10:8: I will signal to them and receive them, for I will redeem them; and they shall be multiplied just as they were many.
verses.10:9: And I will sow them among the peoples, and those who are far off shall remember Me; they shall rear their children and return.
verses.10:10: And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt, and from the Assyrians I will receive them; and into Gilead and into Lebanon I will bring them, and not even one of them shall be left behind.
verses.10:11: And they shall pass through a narrow sea, and they shall strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the rivers shall be dried up; and all the pride of the Assyrians shall be taken away, and the scepter of Egypt shall be removed.
verses.10:12: And I will strengthen them in the Lord their God, and in His name they shall boast," says the Lord.
verses.11:1: Open wide your doors, O Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars.
verses.11:2: Let the pine tree wail, because the cedar has fallen, for the mighty ones have been greatly brought to ruin. Wail, you oaks of Bashan, because the dense forest has been torn down.
verses.11:3: A sound of lamenting shepherds, because their majesty has been brought to ruin; a sound of roaring lions, because the pride of the Jordan has been brought to ruin.
verses.11:4: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Shepherd the sheep of the slaughter,
verses.11:5: whose buyers slaughtered them and felt no remorse, and those who sold them said, 'Blessed be the Lord, and we have become rich'; and their shepherds felt nothing at all for them.
verses.11:6: Therefore I will no longer spare the inhabitants of the land," says the Lord. "And behold, I am delivering men, each into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king; and they shall strike down the land, and I will by no means deliver them out of their hand."
verses.11:7: And I will shepherd the sheep of the slaughter into Canaan; and I will take for myself two staffs—the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Measuring Line—and I will shepherd the sheep.
verses.11:8: And I will remove the three shepherds in one month, and my soul shall be weighed down against them, for their souls also roared against me.
verses.11:9: And I said, "I will not shepherd you. Let what is dying die, and let what is failing fail; and as for the rest, let each devour the flesh of his neighbor."
verses.11:10: And they shall take my beautiful staff, and I will cast it away, to annul my covenant which I made with all the peoples.
verses.11:11: And it shall be annulled in that day, and the Canaanites, the sheep that are kept for me, shall know that it is the word of the Lord.
verses.11:12: And I will say to them, "If it is good in your sight, give my wages, or else refuse." And they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
verses.11:13: And the Lord said to me, "Drop them into the smelting furnace, and I will see whether it is genuine, just as it was tested on their behalf." And I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them into the house of the Lord, into the smelting furnace.
verses.11:14: And I cast away the second staff, Measuring Line, to annul the possession between Judah and Israel.
verses.11:15: And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself yet again the pastoral implements of an inexperienced shepherd.
verses.11:16: For behold, I am raising up a shepherd over the land: what is failing he will by no means visit, and what is scattered he will by no means seek, and what is broken he will by no means heal, and what is whole he will by no means guide aright; yet the flesh of the choice ones he shall devour, and their ankles he shall dislocate.
verses.11:17: Woe to those who shepherd vain things and have forsaken the sheep! A sword upon his arms and upon his right eye! His arm shall surely wither away, and his right eye shall be utterly blinded."
verses.12:1: The burden of the word of the Lord concerning Israel. Says the Lord, who stretches out heaven, and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him:
verses.12:2: "Behold, I am making Jerusalem like shaking doorways to all the peoples round about, and in Judea there shall be a siege against Jerusalem.
verses.12:3: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will make Jerusalem a stone trampled upon by all the nations; everyone who tramples upon her shall surely mock, and all the nations of the earth shall be gathered together against her.
verses.12:4: In that day," says the Lord Almighty, "I will strike every horse with bewilderment and its rider with madness; but upon the house of Judah I will open wide My eyes, and all the horses of the peoples I will strike with blindness.
verses.12:5: And the commanders of thousands of Judah shall say in their hearts, 'We shall find for ourselves the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the Lord Almighty their God.'
verses.12:6: In that day I will make the commanders of thousands of Judah like a firebrand among wood, and like a torch of fire among stubble; and they shall devour on the right hand and on the left all the peoples round about, and Jerusalem shall dwell yet again by herself in Jerusalem.
verses.12:7: And the Lord shall save the tents of Judah as from the beginning, so that the boasting of the house of David and the arrogance of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be magnified above Judah.
verses.12:8: And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the one who is weak among them in that day shall be like David, and the house of David like the house of God, like the angel of the Lord before them.
verses.12:9: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will seek to remove all the nations that come against Jerusalem;
verses.12:10: and I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and compassion; and they shall look upon Me because they danced in mockery, and they shall mourn for Him with mourning as for a beloved one, and they shall grieve with grief as over the firstborn.
verses.12:11: In that day the mourning in Jerusalem shall be magnified like the mourning for a pomegranate grove being cut down in a plain;
verses.12:12: and the land shall mourn, tribe by tribe: the tribe of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the tribe of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.12:13: the tribe of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the tribe of Simeon by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.12:14: all the remaining tribes, every tribe by itself, and their wives by themselves."
verses.13:1: In that day every place shall be opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for removal and for separation.
verses.13:2: "And it shall be in that day," says the Lord of hosts, "that I will utterly destroy the names of the idols from the land, and there shall no longer be any remembrance of them; and I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land."
verses.13:3: And it shall come to pass, if a man still prophesies, then his father and his mother, who gave birth to him, shall say to him, "You shall not live, because you have spoken falsehoods in the name of the Lord." And his father and his mother, who gave birth to him, shall bind him hand and foot when he prophesies.
verses.13:4: And it shall be in that day that the prophets shall be put to shame, each one because of his vision when he prophesies, and they shall put on a garment of hairy skin because they have lied.
verses.13:5: And he shall say, "I am no prophet, for I am a man who tills the ground, because a man fathered me from my youth."
verses.13:6: And one shall say to him, "What are these wounds between your hands?" And he shall say, "Those with which I was wounded in my beloved house."
verses.13:7: "O sword, awake against My shepherds and against a man who is My fellow citizen," says the Lord Almighty. "Strike the shepherds, and draw out the sheep, and I will bring My hand against the little ones."
verses.13:8: "And it shall be in all the land," says the Lord, "that two parts of it shall be utterly destroyed and perish, but the third shall be left in it;
verses.13:9: and I will bring the third through fire, and refine them by fire as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. They shall call upon My name, and I will hear them; and I will say, 'This is My people,' and they shall say, 'The Lord is my God.'"
verses.14:1: Behold, days of the Lord are coming, and your spoils shall be divided within you.
verses.14:2: And I will gather together all nations against Jerusalem for war, and the city shall be taken, and the houses shall be plundered, and the women shall be defiled, and half of the city shall go forth into captivity, but the remnant of My people shall by no means be utterly destroyed from the city.
verses.14:3: And the Lord shall go forth and do battle against those nations, as on the day of His battle in a day of war.
verses.14:4: And His feet shall stand in that day upon the Mount of Olives, which is opposite Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives shall be split, half of it toward the east and the sea—an exceedingly great chasm; and half of the mountain shall lean toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
verses.14:5: And the valley of My mountains shall be blocked up, and the valley of the mountains shall be joined as far as Iasod, and it shall be blocked up just as it was blocked up in the days of the earthquake, in the days of Uzziah king of Judah; and the Lord my God shall come, and all the holy ones with Him.
verses.14:6: And it shall be in that day that there shall be no light, and there shall be both cold and frost;
verses.14:7: it shall be for one day, and that day is known to the Lord—neither day nor night—and toward evening there shall be light.
verses.14:8: And in that day living water shall go forth from Jerusalem, half of it to the first sea, and half of it to the last sea; and in summer and in spring it shall be so.
verses.14:9: And the Lord shall be King over all the earth; in that day the Lord shall be one, and His name one,
verses.14:10: encompassing all the earth and the wilderness from Geba to Rimmon to the south of Jerusalem. But Ramah shall remain in its place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Gate of the Corners, and to the Tower of Hanamel, to the winepress vats of the king.
verses.14:11: They shall dwell in it, and there shall no longer be any curse, and Jerusalem shall dwell in confidence.
verses.14:12: And this shall be the calamity with which the Lord shall strike all the peoples, as many as marched against Jerusalem: their flesh shall melt away while they stand upon their feet, and their eyes shall flow out of their sockets, and their tongue shall melt away in their mouth.
verses.14:13: And it shall be in that day that a great panic from the Lord shall be upon them; and each one shall seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand shall be interlocked with the hand of his neighbor.
verses.14:14: And Judah also shall do battle in Jerusalem, and shall gather the wealth of all the peoples round about—gold and silver and apparel in exceedingly great abundance.
verses.14:15: And this shall be the calamity of the horses, and of the mules, and of the camels, and of the donkeys, and of all the beasts that are in those camps, according to this calamity.
verses.14:16: And it shall come to pass that as many as are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem shall go up year by year to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, and to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.14:17: And it shall come to pass that as many as do not go up from all the tribes of the earth to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty—these also shall be added to those.
verses.14:18: And if the tribe of Egypt does not go up nor come, upon them also shall be the calamity with which the Lord shall strike all the nations, as many as do not go up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.14:19: This shall be the sin of Egypt and the sin of all the nations, as many as do not go up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
verses.14:20: In that day that which is upon the bridle of the horse shall be holy to the Lord Almighty; and the cauldrons in the house of the Lord shall be like bowls before the altar.
verses.14:21: And every cauldron in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holy to the Lord Almighty; and all those who sacrifice shall come and take of them and boil in them; and there shall no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty in that day.

notes.1:3: The Greek alternates between two divine titles here: Kyrios Pantokrator ("the Lord Almighty") and Kyrios ton dynameon ("the Lord of hosts"), both rendering Hebrew Yahweh Sebaoth.
notes.1:6: Unlike the Masoretic Text's rhetorical question, the Septuagint reads an imperative ("receive My words and My statutes") and specifies "by My Spirit" before "to My servants the prophets."
notes.1:8: The Greek reads "the shady mountains" (rather than the Masoretic "myrtle trees in the hollow") and lists four horse colors ("red, speckled gray, spotted, and white") instead of three.
notes.1:15: The Greek participle synepitithemena describes "the nations that join in attacking," in contrast to the Masoretic Text's "nations at ease."
notes.2:1: Chapter 2 in the Septuagint begins at Masoretic 1:18; verses 2:5-17 correspond to Masoretic 2:1-13.
notes.2:4: The Septuagint renders the craftsmen's purpose literally as "to sharpen them into their hands," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants from the Masoretic "to terrify them, to cast down."
notes.2:8: The Greek adverb katakarpos ("fruitfully") renders a Hebrew term that in the Masoretic Text means "as unwalled villages."
notes.2:10: The Septuagint reads the future promise "I will gather you" from the four winds of heaven, whereas the Masoretic Text reads "I have spread you abroad."
notes.2:17: The Greek concludes with "from His holy clouds" (ek nephelon hagion autou), differing from the Masoretic Text's "from His holy dwelling."
notes.3:1: The Greek uses Iesous (rendered with the standard English Old Testament form "Joshua") and translates the adversary's title as ho diabolos ("the devil").
notes.3:4: The Septuagint continues the command to the attendants ("clothe him with a full-length robe [poderes], and set a clean turban upon his head") directly from verse 4 into verse 5 without the Masoretic "And I said."
notes.3:7: This Greek text omits a conditional "if" before the first clause (while retaining "if" before "you diligently guard My court") and renders the final promise as masculine plural anastrephomenous ("those who walk about").
notes.3:8: The Greek describes Joshua's companions as andres teratoskopoi ("men who observe signs") and renders the messianic title as Anatole ("the Dayspring" or "Rising," corresponding to Hebrew "Branch").
notes.3:9: The Septuagint reads "I am digging a pit" and "I will feel out all the unrighteousness," diverging sharply from the Masoretic "I will engrave its inscription" and "I will remove the iniquity."
notes.4:7: The Septuagint differs notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text here, rendering the Hebrew 'into a plain' as the infinitive 'to prosper,' shifting to the first person 'I will bring forth,' and reading 'the stone of the inheritance, an equality of grace' for 'the capstone with shouts of grace.'
notes.4:10: The Greek literally reads 'stone of tin' (for the plumb weight) and speaks simply of 'seven eyes,' without the phrase 'of the Lord' found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:14: 'Sons of fatness' (Greek huioi tes piotetos) is a literal rendering of the Hebrew idiom for those supplied with rich olive oil, signifying the two anointed ones.
notes.5:1: The Septuagint reads 'a flying sickle' (drepanon), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants that the Masoretic Text reads as 'a flying scroll.'
notes.5:6: The Greek renders the Hebrew dry measure ephah as 'measure' and reads 'their iniquity' (he adikia auton) where the Masoretic Text has 'their eye' or 'their appearance.'
notes.5:8: Because Greek metron ('measure') is neuter while the Hebrew ephah is feminine, the Greek feminine pronoun in 'into her mouth' (eis to stoma autes) grammatically aligns with the woman representing lawlessness.
notes.5:9: The Septuagint identifies the bird as a hoopoe (epopos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'stork.'
notes.6:8: The Septuagint opens with the plural 'they cried out' and reads 'My wrath' (ton thumon mou) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'My spirit.'
notes.6:10: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew personal names Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah as descriptive terms ('the rulers,' 'its worthy men,' and 'those who have known it'), a pattern repeated in verse 14.
notes.6:12: The Messianic title 'Dayspring' (Greek Anatole, meaning 'Rising' or 'Shoot,' paired with the verb anatelei, 'shall spring up') translates Hebrew Tzemach ('Branch') and is echoed in Luke 1:78.
notes.6:13: The Septuagint reads 'the priest shall be at His right hand,' placing a distinct priest beside the enthroned ruler, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'he shall be a priest on his throne.'
notes.6:14: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew personal name Hen as 'favor' (charita) and reads 'for a psalm' (eis psalmon) where the Masoretic Text reads 'for a memorial.'
notes.7:2: The Greek text reads "to Bethel" and names "Arbeseer the king," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech").
notes.7:3: The Greek text reads "The sanctification has entered here" (referring to a consecrated offering or observance) rather than the Hebrew question about weeping and fasting.
notes.7:11: Greek "a senseless back" here and "disobedient" in verse 12 reflect distinctive Septuagint renderings where the Hebrew has "a stubborn shoulder" and a heart "like flint."
notes.8:6: The Greek verb literally means "shall it be impossible," rendering the Hebrew sense of being too difficult or wonderful in terms of impossibility.
notes.8:8: The Greek text has the first-person singular "I will dwell" (referring to the Lord), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the third-person plural "they shall dwell."
notes.8:12: The Greek text reads "but rather I will show peace," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("for the seed shall be peaceful").
notes.8:21: The Septuagint specifies "the inhabitants of five cities" assembling into "one city," whereas the Hebrew reads "the inhabitants of one city shall go to another."
notes.9:1: The Greek preserves the distinct place name "Sedrach" (Hebrew "Hadrach") and renders "Damascus is His sacrifice," reflecting a reading of "offering" rather than the Hebrew "resting place."
notes.9:9: The Septuagint reads "proclaim aloud" (rather than "shout"), uses the active participle "saving," and describes the mount simply as "a beast of burden and a young colt."
notes.9:10: The Greek uses the third-person "He shall utterly destroy" and reads "abundance and peace from the nations," differing from the Hebrew ("I will cut off" and "he shall speak peace to the nations").
notes.9:12: The Greek reads "You shall dwell in strongholds, O prisoners of the congregation, and in place of one day of your sojourning," diverging from the Hebrew ("Return to the stronghold, O prisoners of hope; even today I declare").
notes.9:16: The Septuagint renders "holy stones are rolled upon His land," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of "jewels of a crown" gleaming over His land.
notes.10:2: The Greek text reads "withered away" and "no healing," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "wandered" and "no shepherd."
notes.10:3: The Greek reads "the lambs" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the male goats" (leaders).
notes.10:4: The Greek renders the opening clauses with verbs ("from him He looked, and from him He arrayed") and "a bow in wrath," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("cornerstone," "tent peg," "battle bow").
notes.10:10: The Greek concludes "and not even one of them shall be left behind," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "until no room is found for them."
notes.11:7: The Greek reads "into Canaan" (and "the Canaanites" in verse 11), reflecting a different division of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text ("therefore, O afflicted of the flock"). The staff names translate Greek Kallos ("Beauty") and Schoinisma ("Measuring Line").
notes.11:10: The critical Greek text reads the third-person plural future "they shall take" (lempsontai) before shifting to the first person "I will cast it away."
notes.11:13: The Greek reads "smelting furnace" (choneuterion) rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "potter," and uses the third-person passive "it was tested" (edokimasthe) in keeping with the assaying of silver.
notes.11:14: The Greek reads "the possession" (kataschesin) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the brotherhood."
notes.12:2: The Greek renders the image as "shaking doorways" (prothyra saleuomena), taking the underlying Hebrew word in the sense of "threshold" rather than "cup" as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.12:3: The Greek reads "a stone trampled upon" and "shall surely mock" (empaizon empaixetai), diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "heavy stone" and "will surely cut themselves."
notes.12:10: The Greek reads "a spirit of grace and compassion" and "because they danced in mockery" (katorchesanto, reflecting a transposition of Hebrew consonants), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text (and John 19:37) reads "whom they pierced."
notes.12:11: The Greek reads "for a pomegranate grove being cut down in a plain," translating the place names Hadadrimmon and Megiddo of the Hebrew Masoretic Text as common nouns and a participle.
notes.12:13: The Greek reads "the tribe of Simeon" (tou Symeon) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the family of the Shimeites."
notes.13:1: The Septuagint reads "every place" (reflecting a reading of Hebrew maqom rather than maqor, "fountain") and "for removal and for separation," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a fountain... for sin and for uncleanness."
notes.13:3: The Greek verb sympodizo means "to bind hand and foot" (or tie the feet together), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "thrust through" or "pierce."
notes.13:4: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("they shall not wear a hairy mantle to deceive"), the Greek omits the negative and states that the shamed prophets "shall put on a garment of hairy skin because they have lied."
notes.13:7: The Septuagint reads plural "My shepherds" and active plural imperatives ("Strike the shepherds, and draw out the sheep"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a singular shepherd and a passive verb ("the sheep shall be scattered").
notes.14:5: The Greek reads "shall be blocked up" twice where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "flee," and preserves the distinct place name Iasod where the Hebrew reads Azel.
notes.14:6: The Septuagint reads "cold and frost" (psyche kai pagos) continuing into "for one day" (mian hemeran) in verse 7, diverging from the difficult phrasing of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.14:8: The Greek reads "in summer and in spring" (en eari) rather than "in summer and in winter," and translates the eastern and western seas literally as "the first sea" and "the last sea."
notes.14:10: The Septuagint reads "encompassing all the earth and the wilderness," takes Ramah as a proper name rather than a verb ("shall be lifted up"), and reads Hanamel (Anameel) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Hananel.
notes.14:17: The Greek concludes with "these also shall be added to those" (that is, counted among the afflicted nations), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "upon them there shall be no rain."
